seo.meta_title: '저희 나라' or '우리나라'? | The Humble Form AI Overuses
seo.meta_description: AI often makes 'our country' extra polite as '저희 나라' — but Koreans say '우리나라' even in formal speech. Here's why.

ai_failure.situation: Politely telling a Korean person something about Korea, e.g. 'In our country, we eat rice cake soup on New Year's.'
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Uses '저희 나라' because 저희 is the humble form of 'we/our' and the sentence is polite.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: Humbling your own nation in front of fellow Koreans makes no sense — the listener belongs to the same country. Standard guidance treats 우리나라 as correct even in formal speech.

natural_solution.rule: Say 우리나라 (or 한국) for Korea in every register. Use 저희 only for groups the listener is not part of — your company, your family, your team.

alternatives.context: Talking about Korea, polite and natural
Correct use of 저희 — the listener isn't part of your company

nuance: 저희 lowers the speaker's group relative to the listener, so it only works when the listener stands outside that group. A nation is a group every Korean listener shares, so 우리나라 is written as a single word and used by presidents and news anchors alike. The trap shows how Korean politeness isn't a dial you simply turn up — it depends on who is inside and who is outside the 'we'.
